title: AIW Budget Policy
description: Spend policy for the AIW provider router — the file that decides how much real money one AFK cycle may spend. additionalProperties is false at every level so an unrecognized key is a load error, not a silent no-op.

schema_version.description: Pinned deliberately — a version bump must arrive with a schema change, not on its own

cycle.description: Aggregate caps across all packets in one cycle

max_cost_usd.description: Total USD one cycle may reserve plus spend

max_parallel_packets.description: Concurrent reservations allowed in the cycle ledger

defaults.description: Per-job ceilings. A job request may tighten these (see _cap) but never widen them.

max_retries.description: Zero is a legitimate tightening (no retries), so this bound is inclusive unlike the other caps

approval_required_above_usd.description: Estimated cost above this needs a bound human-approval artifact

providers.description: The allowlist. _provider() rejects any id absent from this list.

trusted_receipt_issuer.description: Hostname that must issue the release receipt; only meaningful for metered-cloud

allOf.description: A metered provider bills real money: it must name a receipt issuer and require approval, because _validate_receipt refuses a null issuer and release() cannot reconcile without one.
A local-seat provider costs no metered money and has no receipt to trust.

selection_order.description: Router preference order. Entries must be declared provider ids — that cross-reference is enforced in load_policy(), which JSON Schema cannot express.
